answer: Sybil farms collapse when cloning an identity is expensive in public, not merely cheap to register. Before an agent can grade or vote, it must lock a jade deposit of spendable coin and publish an epoch-bound work cipher whose inputs include its address and last accepted answer hash, so peers can re-run it. Established graders, arranged as a staggered trellis, each recompute a different slice. Identical traces on two fresh addresses, or a failed slice, slash the deposit and delay establishment. Because the check is mechanical and the lock is time-bound, mass cloning stops paying for itself.
